label: Luke 8:1
text: Soon afterwards, he went about through cities and villages, preaching and bringing the good news of God’s Kingdom. With him were the twelve,

label: Luke 8:2
text: and certain women who had been healed of evil spirits and infirmities: Mary who was called Magdalene, from whom seven demons had gone out;

label: Luke 8:3
text: and Joanna, the wife of Chuzas, Herod’s steward; Susanna; and many others; who served them from their possessions.

label: Luke 8:4
text: When a great multitude came together, and people from every city were coming to him, he spoke by a parable.

label: Luke 8:5
text: “The farmer went out to sow his seed. As he sowed, some fell along the road, and it was trampled under foot, and the birds of the sky devoured it.

label: Luke 8:6
text: Other seed fell on the rock, and as soon as it grew, it withered away, because it had no moisture.

label: Luke 8:7
text: Other fell amid the thorns, and the thorns grew with it, and choked it.

label: Luke 8:8
text:
Other fell into the good ground, and grew, and produced one hundred times as much fruit.” As he said these things, he called out,
“He who has ears to hear, let him hear!”

label: Luke 8:9
text: Then his disciples asked him, “What does this parable mean?”

label: Luke 8:10
text:
He said,
“To you it is given to know the mysteries of God’s Kingdom, but to the rest in parables; that ‘seeing they may not see, and hearing they may not understand.’

label: Luke 8:11
text: Now the parable is this: The seed is the word of God.

label: Luke 8:12
text: Those along the road are those who hear, then the devil comes, and takes away the word from their heart, that they may not believe and be saved.

label: Luke 8:13
text: Those on the rock are they who, when they hear, receive the word with joy; but these have no root, who believe for a while, then fall away in time of temptation.

label: Luke 8:14
text: That which fell among the thorns, these are those who have heard, and as they go on their way they are choked with cares, riches, and pleasures of life, and bring no fruit to maturity.

label: Luke 8:15
text: Those in the good ground, these are those who with an honest and good heart, having heard the word, hold it tightly, and produce fruit with perseverance.

label: Luke 8:16
text: “No one, when he has lit a lamp, covers it with a container, or puts it under a bed; but puts it on a stand, that those who enter in may see the light.

label: Luke 8:17
text: For nothing is hidden, that will not be revealed; nor anything secret, that will not be known and come to light.

label: Luke 8:18
text: Be careful therefore how you hear. For whoever has, to him will be given; and whoever doesn’t have, from him will be taken away even that which he thinks he has.”

label: Luke 8:19
text: His mother and brothers came to him, and they could not come near him for the crowd.

label: Luke 8:20
text: Some people told him, “Your mother and your brothers stand outside, desiring to see you.”

label: Luke 8:21
text:
But he answered them,
“My mother and my brothers are these who hear the word of God, and do it.”

label: Luke 8:22
text:
Now on one of those days, he entered into a boat, himself and his disciples, and he said to them,
“Let’s go over to the other side of the lake.” So they launched out.

label: Luke 8:23
text: But as they sailed, he fell asleep. A wind storm came down on the lake, and they were taking on dangerous amounts of water.

label: Luke 8:24
text: They came to him, and awoke him, saying, “Master, master, we are dying!” He awoke, and rebuked the wind and the raging of the water, and they ceased, and it was calm.

label: Luke 8:25
text:
He said to them,
“Where is your faith?” Being afraid they marveled, saying to one another, “Who is this then, that he commands even the winds and the water, and they obey him?”

label: Luke 8:26
text: They arrived at the country of the Gadarenes, which is opposite Galilee.

variants.note: Also D and Uncial 0267; the Latin and Coptic witnesses (Wikipedia, Textual variants in the Gospel of Luke, Luke 8:26). The WEB follows the Byzantine 'Gadarenes'.
Also L, X, Theta, Xi, family 1, 22, 33, 157, 579, 700*, 1241, 1342, Syriac, Eusebius and Epiphanius (Wikipedia, Textual variants in the Gospel of Luke, Luke 8:26).
A, R, W, Delta, Psi, Uncial 0135, family 13, 700c, 1071, Byzantine text, Gothic (Wikipedia, Textual variants in the Gospel of Luke, Luke 8:26); no graph manuscript carries it as its main reading.

label: Luke 8:27
text: When Jesus stepped ashore, a certain man out of the city who had demons for a long time met him. He wore no clothes, and didn’t live in a house, but in the tombs.

label: Luke 8:28
text: When he saw Jesus, he cried out, and fell down before him, and with a loud voice said, “What do I have to do with you, Jesus, you Son of the Most High God? I beg you, don’t torment me!”

label: Luke 8:29
text: For Jesus was commanding the unclean spirit to come out of the man. For the unclean spirit had often seized the man. He was kept under guard, and bound with chains and fetters. Breaking the bonds apart, he was driven by the demon into the desert.

label: Luke 8:30
text:
Jesus asked him,
“What is your name?”
He said, “Legion,” for many demons had entered into him.

label: Luke 8:31
text: They begged him that he would not command them to go into the abyss.

label: Luke 8:32
text: Now there was there a herd of many pigs feeding on the mountain, and they begged him that he would allow them to enter into those. He allowed them.

label: Luke 8:33
text: The demons came out of the man, and entered into the pigs, and the herd rushed down the steep bank into the lake, and were drowned.

label: Luke 8:34
text: When those who fed them saw what had happened, they fled, and told it in the city and in the country.

label: Luke 8:35
text: People went out to see what had happened. They came to Jesus, and found the man from whom the demons had gone out, sitting at Jesus’ feet, clothed and in his right mind; and they were afraid.

label: Luke 8:36
text: Those who saw it told them how he who had been possessed by demons was healed.

label: Luke 8:37
text: All the people of the surrounding country of the Gadarenes asked him to depart from them, for they were very much afraid. He entered into the boat, and returned.

label: Luke 8:38
text: But the man from whom the demons had gone out begged him that he might go with him, but Jesus sent him away, saying,

label: Luke 8:39
text: “Return to your house, and declare what great things God has done for you.” He went his way, proclaiming throughout the whole city what great things Jesus had done for him.

label: Luke 8:40
text: When Jesus returned, the multitude welcomed him, for they were all waiting for him.

label: Luke 8:41
text: Behold, there came a man named Jairus, and he was a ruler of the synagogue. He fell down at Jesus’ feet, and begged him to come into his house,

label: Luke 8:42
text: for he had an only daughter, about twelve years of age, and she was dying. But as he went, the multitudes pressed against him.

label: Luke 8:43
text: A woman who had a flow of blood for twelve years, who had spent all her living on physicians, and could not be healed by any,

variants.reading: ιατροις προσαναλωσασα ολον το βιον ('and had spent all her living upon physicians') absent
variants.note: Omitted by P75, B, (D), 0279, syr s,pal, Coptic, Armenian, Georgian and Origen; included by the Byzantine text. The WEB keeps it (Wikipedia, Textual variants in the Gospel of Luke, Luke 8:43).

label: Luke 8:44
text: came behind him, and touched the fringe of his cloak, and immediately the flow of her blood stopped.

label: Luke 8:45
text:
Jesus said,
“Who touched me?”
When all denied it, Peter and those with him said, “Master, the multitudes press and jostle you, and you say,
‘Who touched me?’”

variants.reading: εἶπεν ὁ Πέτρος ('Peter said') — only Peter
variants.note: Alexandrian text-type reads 'Peter said'; the expansion 'Peter and those with him said' (followed by the WEB) belongs to other witnesses (Wikipedia, Textual variants in the Gospel of Luke, Luke 8:45); no graph manuscript listed.

label: Luke 8:46
text:
But Jesus said,
“Someone did touch me, for I perceived that power has gone out of me.”

label: Luke 8:47
text: When the woman saw that she was not hidden, she came trembling, and falling down before him declared to him in the presence of all the people the reason why she had touched him, and how she was healed immediately.

label: Luke 8:48
text:
He said to her,
“Daughter, cheer up. Your faith has made you well. Go in peace.”

label: Luke 8:49
text: While he still spoke, one from the ruler of the synagogue’s house came, saying to him, “Your daughter is dead. Don’t trouble the Teacher.”

label: Luke 8:50
text:
But Jesus hearing it, answered him,
“Don’t be afraid. Only believe, and she will be healed.”

label: Luke 8:51
text: When he came to the house, he didn’t allow anyone to enter in, except Peter, John, James, the father of the child, and her mother.

label: Luke 8:52
text:
All were weeping and mourning her, but he said,
“Don’t weep. She isn’t dead, but sleeping.”

label: Luke 8:53
text: They were ridiculing him, knowing that she was dead.

label: Luke 8:54
text:
But he put them all outside, and taking her by the hand, he called, saying,
“Child, arise!”

variants.reading: αὐτὸς δὲ κρατήσας τῆς χειρὸς αὐτῆς ('but he took her by the hand') without 'he put them all outside'
variants.note: Alexandrian text-type; the WEB's 'he put them all outside, and taking her by the hand' is Byzantine (Wikipedia, Textual variants in the Gospel of Luke, Luke 8:54); no graph manuscript listed.

label: Luke 8:55
text: Her spirit returned, and she rose up immediately. He commanded that something be given to her to eat.

label: Luke 8:56
text: Her parents were amazed, but he commanded them to tell no one what had been done.

label: Women healed by Jesus travelled with the Twelve and provided for them
statement: Certain women healed of evil spirits and infirmities - Mary called Magdalene, Joanna, Susanna and many others - accompanied Jesus and the Twelve and served them from their possessions.

label: Mary Magdalene delivered of seven demons
statement: Mary, called Magdalene, had been healed of evil spirits and infirmities, from whom seven demons had gone out.

label: Joanna the wife of Chuza among the women
statement: Joanna, the wife of Chuza, was one of the women who followed Jesus and provided for the group.
note: Luke names her only here and at Luke 24:10.

label: Chuza was Herod's steward (epitropos)
statement: Chuza, Joanna's husband, held the office of steward (epitropos) of Herod Antipas - manager of the tetrarch's household and estates.

label: Isaiah 6:9-10 quoted on seeing and not perceiving
statement: Jesus quotes Isaiah 6:9-10 ('seeing they may not see, and hearing they may not understand') to explain why he speaks to outsiders in parables.
note: Matthew cites the same passage at 13:14-15; the Gospels are not independent evidence for each other.

label: Hearers of the word called mother and brothers
statement: Jesus answered that his mother and his brothers are those who hear the word of God and do it.

label: The healed Gerasene sent home to proclaim in his city
statement: The delivered man begged to go with Jesus; Jesus sent him home with the charge 'Return to your house, and declare what great things God has done for you', and he proclaimed it throughout the whole city.
note: Mark 5:19-20 sends him through the Decapolis; Luke keeps him in his city. Related difference, not evidence.

label: Jairus's only daughter, about twelve, dying
statement: Jairus had an only daughter, about twelve years of age, who was dying; as Jesus went, the crowds pressed on him.
note: Mark 5:23 says the girl was at the point of death; Mark 5:42 says she was twelve.

label: Peter, John, James and the parents inside the house
statement: At the house Jesus allowed no one to enter except Peter, John and James, and the child's father and mother.
note: Mark 5:37 names only Peter, James and John following in; Luke admits the parents too and orders John before James.

label: Household and neighbours weeping and mourning over the girl
statement: All were weeping and mourning the girl; Jesus said she was not dead but sleeping, and they ridiculed him, knowing that she was dead.
note: Matthew 9:23 adds the flute players of professional mourning; Luke mentions only the weeping crowd.

label: The exorcism set in the country of the Gadarenes, opposite Galilee
statement: Luke 8:26 sets the event in the country of the Gadarenes, which is opposite Galilee.
note: Manuscripts read Gerasenes (P75, B, D), Gergesenes (Sinaiticus and others) or Gadarenes (A, W, Byz; the WEB); Matthew 8:28 reads Gergesenes/Gadarenes and Mark 5:1 Gadarenes/Gerasenes; the site is disputed (Gadara, Gerasa, Hippos, Kursi).

label: Susanna (one of the women who followed Jesus)
